relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with Blau syndrome carrying a NOD2 variant: 'showing an heterozygous c.1001G>A, p.Arg334Gln mutation (R334Q) in NOD2'.
method_note: Hand-extracted from a short single-patient case report (no tables, no supplement). Only one in-scope person; the mother is mentioned only as recalling the rash history and is not described as tested or affected, so she gets no row. Age 7 years is the age at referral to the authors' clinic, not at last evaluation, and no age is given for the Blau diagnosis (age 2 was the earlier, revised JIA diagnosis), so both are 'not reported'. Vital status 'alive' is read from the present-tense statement of current treatment. Pathogenicity is the authors' wording 'known to be linked to Blau syndrome' (no formal class). Variant type is not stated (not derived from HGVS). 'The opthalmology exam was normal' at referral is recorded as written ('abnormal ophthalmology exam' excluded) and does not exclude uveitis; uveitis was found later by slit-lamp, so not treated as a contradiction. 'Non-deforming' polyarticular involvement is recorded as deforming joint involvement excluded; camptodactyly left 'not reported'. Laboratory values at referral (WBC 12600/μL, CRP 10mg/l, ESR 40mm/h) are not called abnormal by the authors and were not recorded as features. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null because the paper says nothing about earlier reports. No contradictions found.

span: her treatment included methotrexate, etanercept and prednisolone with only mild alleviation of symptoms
the patient was started on tocilizumab for 4 months, which led to insignificant clinical improvement
In combination with three methylprednisolone pulses and gradual steroid reduction, we initiated therapy with canakinumab leading to a prompt clinical improvement
After 12 months on canakinumab monotherapy, she was in complete clinical and laboratory remission
At the moment she is steroid dependent, and her treatment includes adalimumab and methotrexate
